Name: kuairand_fm_validation_baseline
Title: Autonomous Improvement of Long-View Ranking on KuaiRand-Pure
Short Hypothesis: A validation-only autonomous experiment loop can reliably reproduce the organizer FM baseline before attempting controlled ranking improvements.
Related Work: Factorization Machines provide the organizer baseline. AI Scientist-v2 provides staged experiment management and tree search. The initial deployment focuses on a trustworthy connection between them.
Abstract: Build an autonomous research workflow around the organizer-provided KuaiRand-Pure Starter Kit. The first stage must reproduce the fixed Factorization Machine baseline using long_view as the relevance label and validation primary=(GAUC+nDCG@5)/2 as the only node-selection score. The workflow must preserve the official chronological split and evaluator, use no external training dataset, and expose no test feedback during research. Later stages may tune the fixed FM and explore controlled ranking improvements after the baseline connection is verified. Data priors from population-level EDA on the official training split (leakage-safe; machine-readable facts in input/data_analysis/eda_summary.json): (1) cold-start is negligible, with unseen video/author about 0.01 percent, so content or ID-fallback features are low-value; (2) nDCG@5 is structurally capped near 0.73 on both valid and test because roughly 27 percent of users are all-negative and score nDCG=0 in the mean, so gains should target GAUC rather than nDCG; (3) the tab field's positive rate spans an order of magnitude (about 0.4 percent to 49 percent), making tab-by-user and tab-by-video crosses high-value, whereas pure user-side first-order terms add the same constant to every impression of a user and cannot change within-user order; (4) pointwise log loss is misaligned with the ranking metric, so a within-user pairwise or BPR objective is the highest-priority first move. Any temporal or statistical feature must be constructed causally from strictly earlier events only.
Experiments: Execute the supplied editable CandidateModel program directly as the Stage 1 baseline; do not replace it with or invoke the legacy run_fm_experiment.py CLI.
Verify finite predictions, the official validation GAUC and nDCG@5, primary computation, early stopping, checkpoint creation, and protected-file hashes.
Accept Stage 1 only if the supplied program writes working/experiment_data.npy and primary reproduces the published baseline within expected seed variation.

Data-prior-driven priority (Stage 3): replace pointwise log loss with a within-user pairwise/BPR objective first, since the metric is ranking-based and GAUC carries the larger headroom; compare one vs several negatives per positive and random vs popularity-aware sampling under equal budget.

Data-prior-driven priority (Stage 3): add tab-by-user and tab-by-video cross features (tab positive rate spans an order of magnitude); do not rely on pure user-side first-order terms, which cannot reorder a user's own impressions.
Data-prior-driven exclusion: do not invest in cold-start or content-fallback features; unseen video/author is about 0.01 percent, so there are almost no cold-start rows to help.

Leakage guard for any temporal or rolling-statistic feature: build it only from events strictly earlier than the scored impression, and reject any feature whose timestamp provenance cannot be verified.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The research loop must not use validation labels as features, test labels or metrics as feedback, external training datasets, altered evaluator logic, or noncausal temporal features. A full autonomous run also requires a configured supported LLM provider or a compatible local Ollama model.
